findings.issue_text: [Medium/bug] AssertEvents.java:~480 — isAccessTokenId matcher is a no-op: uses items[0].substring(3, 5) (wrong slice, grant shortcut is at indices 4–5) and the comparison is inverted (returns false when the shortcut matches), so the matcher accepts any 6-char prefix and the updated event assertions verify nothing

[Medium/bug] AccessTokenContext.java:~75 — Copy-paste bug in constructor: Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, ...) is duplicated; the second call should validate rawTokenId, so a null rawTokenId is silently accepted and produces an "onrtrt:null"-style token ID downstream

[Medium/api] OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.java — getShortcut() was added to the interface without a default implementation, breaking compilation/linking of existing third-party OAuth2GrantTypeFactory implementations; provide a default method (e.g., returning a derived/UNKNOWN shortcut)

[Medium/data] DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java:postInit — Duplicate-shortcut validation is incomplete: it does not detect a grant ID colliding with another grant's shortcut, a shortcut equal to the reserved "na" (UNKNOWN) marker, or a shortcut colliding with "un"-style prefixes, any of which silently produces ambiguous token-ID encodings/decodings

[Medium/data] OAuth2GrantTypeBase.java:109 / TokenManager.java:248 — Constants.GRANT_TYPE resolves to "grant_type" (same as the OAuth2 form parameter) and is written into client-session context; since client-session attributes persist beyond the request, a stale grant type from the flow that created the session can leak into token IDs generated later from the same session; a namespaced key (e.g., "req-aud" style) would be safer

[Low/concurrency] DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java — grantsByShortcuts/grantsToShortcuts are plain non-volatile fields assigned in postInit and lazily mutated from request threads, an unsafe publication/visibility risk, and the check-then-act lazy-refresh sequences are not atomic so the two maps can transiently diverge

[Low/performance] DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java:getGrantTypeByShortcut — Unknown-shortcut lookups fall back to a full stream iteration over OAuth2GrantType provider factories (and getShortcutByGrantType does a provider-factory lookup); if getTokenContextFromTokenId is called on untrusted/malformed token IDs this becomes a repeated full-scan hot path with no negative caching

[Low/security] DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:getTokenContextFromTokenId — Throws raw IllegalArgumentException for malformed/unknown token-ID prefixes; since token IDs can come from attacker-supplied tokens (introspection/validation paths), callers must translate these into 400-class OAuth errors rather than leaking stack traces/500s, and no such handling is established in this PR

[Low/bug] OAuth2GrantType.java:Context — grantType is captured once in the constructor from formParams, but the class also exposes setFormParams(...); if form params are replaced after construction, the cached grantType becomes stale and out of sync with the actual params

[Low/test_gap] DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest.java — Unit test mutates factory maps by hand and never exercises postInit shortcut-collision validation, the lazy-refresh paths (getShortcutByGrantType/getGrantTypeByShortcut with a live KeycloakSessionFactory), or the case where GRANT_TYPE attribute is absent from a real ClientSessionContext; also no integration coverage that an issued access token's encoded ID round-trips through refresh/introspection end-to-end

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/api] OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.java — getShortcut() was added to the interface without a default implementation, breaking compilation/linking of existing third-party OAuth2GrantTypeFactory implementations; provide a default method (e.g., returning a derived/UNKNOWN shortcut)

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new abstract method `String getShortcut();` to the `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` interface (server-spi-private) without providing a default implementation. While this PR updates Keycloak’s own implementations to implement it, any existing third-party `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` implementations (compiled against the old interface) would fail to compile on upgrade and/or throw `AbstractMethodError` at runtime due to the missing method. This is a concrete API/binary compatibility break introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/data] DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java:postInit — Duplicate-shortcut validation is incomplete: it does not detect a grant ID colliding with another grant's shortcut, a shortcut equal to the reserved "na" (UNKNOWN) marker, or a shortcut colliding with "un"-style prefixes, any of which silently produces ambiguous token-ID encodings/decodings

adjudication.rationale: In `postInit`, the code builds two inverse maps (`grantsByShortcuts` and `grantsToShortcuts`) and then validates uniqueness by comparing their sizes; this *does* detect duplicate shortcuts or duplicate IDs because one of the maps would overwrite an entry and the sizes would diverge, triggering the `IllegalStateException`. The alleged “grant ID colliding with another grant’s shortcut” is not an ambiguity in this encoding/decoding scheme because decoding uses only the shortcut->grantType map and encoding uses only the grantType->shortcut map; overlap between a string used as an ID and a different string used as a shortcut does not create an ambiguous token format. The claim about collisions with `un`-style prefixes is also unfounded because sessionType/tokenType/grantType occupy fixed 2-character positions in a 6-character prefix, so reuse of values across positions is not ambiguous. The only partially plausible edge case (a custom grant using reserved UNKNOWN marker `na`) is not shown in the diff and is already caught unless both its ID and shortcut are exactly `na`, which is hypothetical and not evidenced here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/data] OAuth2GrantTypeBase.java:109 / TokenManager.java:248 — Constants.GRANT_TYPE resolves to "grant_type" (same as the OAuth2 form parameter) and is written into client-session context; since client-session attributes persist beyond the request, a stale grant type from the flow that created the session can leak into token IDs generated later from the same session; a namespaced key (e.g., "req-aud" style) would be safer

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add `Constants.GRANT_TYPE = OAuth2Constants.GRANT_TYPE` (likely the literal "grant_type") and stores it via `clientSessionCtx.setAttribute(Constants.GRANT_TYPE, ...)` in several flows. However, the finding’s core claim—that “client-session attributes persist beyond the request” and therefore a stale grant type can leak into later token IDs from the same session—is not verifiable from this diff. The changes shown only interact with `ClientSessionContext` (an in-memory context wrapper) and do not show any persistence of this attribute into the underlying session/notes across requests, nor any demonstrated reuse that would cause staleness. The namespacing concern is also speculative given no conflicting use is shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/concurrency] DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java — grantsByShortcuts/grantsToShortcuts are plain non-volatile fields assigned in postInit and lazily mutated from request threads, an unsafe publication/visibility risk, and the check-then-act lazy-refresh sequences are not atomic so the two maps can transiently diverge

adjudication.rationale: In DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory, the maps grantsByShortcuts/grantsToShortcuts are assigned in postInit (as new ConcurrentHashMap<>()) and later mutated from getShortcutByGrantType()/getGrantTypeByShortcut() on demand. While the maps themselves are concurrent, updates are performed as separate put() calls to two different maps, so they can be temporarily inconsistent under concurrency. The finding’s broader “unsafe publication/visibility risk” is plausible because the fields are non-final/non-volatile and written outside the constructor, but the diff alone doesn’t prove the factory isn’t safely published by the framework before use; so it’s a concrete concurrency/robustness concern, not a clearly verifiable defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/performance] DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java:getGrantTypeByShortcut — Unknown-shortcut lookups fall back to a full stream iteration over OAuth2GrantType provider factories (and getShortcutByGrantType does a provider-factory lookup); if getTokenContextFromTokenId is called on untrusted/malformed token IDs this becomes a repeated full-scan hot path with no negative caching

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory#getGrantTypeByShortcut and #getShortcutByGrantType. Both methods perform potentially expensive refresh logic on cache misses: getGrantTypeByShortcut does a full provider-factory stream scan (sessionFactory.getProviderFactoriesStream(OAuth2GrantType.class) ... filter by shortcut) when a shortcut is not found, and does not negative-cache unknown shortcuts; getShortcutByGrantType does a provider-factory lookup on miss (sessionFactory.getProviderFactory(OAuth2GrantType.class, grantType)). Since DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider#getTokenContextFromTokenId calls getGrantTypeByShortcut for every parsed token id, malformed/untrusted token IDs with unknown shortcuts could repeatedly trigger these miss paths, creating a repeated scan hot path. This is a concrete performance/DoS-resilience concern introduced by the new code, but not a functional correctness bug by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/security] DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:getTokenContextFromTokenId — Throws raw IllegalArgumentException for malformed/unknown token-ID prefixes; since token IDs can come from attacker-supplied tokens (introspection/validation paths), callers must translate these into 400-class OAuth errors rather than leaking stack traces/500s, and no such handling is established in this PR

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider#getTokenContextFromTokenId which throws IllegalArgumentException for malformed token IDs (e.g., wrong length, unknown shortcuts) and does not provide any error-mapping mechanism itself. This is a concrete, diff-grounded robustness/handling concern because the new logic explicitly throws on parse failures, but the diff does not show any caller-side translation to OAuth/HTTP 4xx errors. However, the finding’s claim that this will leak stack traces/500s on attacker-supplied tokens in introspection/validation paths is not verifiable from the provided diff because no call sites for getTokenContextFromTokenId are shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] OAuth2GrantType.java:Context — grantType is captured once in the constructor from formParams, but the class also exposes setFormParams(...); if form params are replaced after construction, the cached grantType becomes stale and out of sync with the actual params

adjudication.rationale: In OAuth2GrantType.Context, the new field `grantType` is initialized only once in the constructor via `formParams.getFirst(OAuth2Constants.GRANT_TYPE)`, but the class still exposes `setFormParams(...)` which can replace `this.formParams` later without updating `grantType`. Since `getGrantType()` is now used downstream (e.g., OAuth2GrantTypeBase sets `clientSessionCtx` attribute from `context.getGrantType()`), changing form params after construction can make `grantType` stale and inconsistent with the actual `formParams` stored in the context.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/test_gap] DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest.java — Unit test mutates factory maps by hand and never exercises postInit shortcut-collision validation, the lazy-refresh paths (getShortcutByGrantType/getGrantTypeByShortcut with a live KeycloakSessionFactory), or the case where GRANT_TYPE attribute is absent from a real ClientSessionContext; also no integration coverage that an issued access token's encoded ID round-trips through refresh/introspection end-to-end

adjudication.rationale: The new unit test `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest` constructs `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory` and then directly assigns `factory.grantsByShortcuts`/`factory.grantsToShortcuts` by hand, never invoking `postInit(...)` (where shortcut-collision validation and sessionFactory-backed population occurs). As a result it does not exercise the lazy-refresh logic in `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.getShortcutByGrantType(...)` / `getGrantTypeByShortcut(...)` that depends on a live `KeycloakSessionFactory`, nor does it cover the `getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext(...)` path when `clientSessionContext.getAttribute(Constants.GRANT_TYPE, ...)` is null (the provider substitutes `UNKNOWN`). These are concrete, newly added nontrivial behaviors in the diff that are not covered by the added test, but this is a test gap rather than a verifiable functional defect.
